EmptyState.journeyHeading: How Hermes works, step by step
EmptyState.journeyDescription: From the moment you activate your agent to the brief waiting on your phone tomorrow morning.
EmptyState.journeyStep1Body: One click from your Sokosumi account. No installs, no API keys to manage. Hermes is bound to your account from this moment on.
EmptyState.journeyStep2Body: A private computer spins up just for you. Your notes and settings stay put, passwords are locked away, and nothing is shared with anyone else.
EmptyState.journeyStep3Body: Sign in to Gmail, Outlook, Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear, GitHub and more. Your credentials never touch Sokosumi — they stay only on your computer.
EmptyState.journeyStep4Body: Hermes scans your inbox, looks at your calendar, syncs your Sokosumi jobs, and builds a private memory of who and what matters.
EmptyState.journeyStep5Body: Ask in plain language. Hermes picks the right tool, drafts the email, opens the ticket, hires a Sokosumi specialist agent when needed. And brings the result back.
EmptyState.journeyStep6Body: Tell Hermes when to run things. In plain English. Briefings, follow-ups, overnight digests land in chat (and on Telegram or Slack) before you wake up.
EmptyState.feature1Body: Context across every session. No re-explaining.
EmptyState.feature2Body: Pulls in any Sokosumi agent on demand.
EmptyState.feature3Body: Chat here, Telegram, Slack, or wherever you work.
EmptyState.feature4Body: Isolated by default. Your data stays yours.
EmptyState.feature5Body: Daily briefs, follow-ups, reminders. Set once.
EmptyState.feature6Body: Mail, calendar, CRM, code, docs. All in one chat.
EmptyState.examplesHelp: Open the chat and ask anything. A few starting points:
EmptyState.example1: Find every email about the Cardano deal, hire the Research agent to profile their team, and brief me before the Friday call.
EmptyState.example1Reply:
Pulling the Cardano thread now. 14 emails since Sept across Alex, legal, and finance. Hiring **Research** (12 credits) on the four people who'll be on Friday's call: backgrounds, recent moves, mutual contacts.

ETA ~15 min. I'll drop a one-page brief here + email it to you 30 min before the call.
EmptyState.example2: Hire the Competitor Research agent on the company Maya emailed me about, then draft a follow-up reply once it's back.
EmptyState.example2Reply:
Found Maya's email. Subject: "What do you make of Nevermind Labs?". Hiring **Competitor Research** (18 credits) with the brief: product, traction, funding, GTM, overlap with our roadmap.

When it's back I'll draft your reply with the top three takeaways inline and queue it in your drafts for review.
EmptyState.example3: Every weekday at 8am, hire the Brief agent on yesterday's inbox + today's calendar and post the summary to Slack #me.
EmptyState.example3Reply:
Scheduled. Every weekday at 08:00 I'll:

1. Pull every email since 20:00 the prior day and your calendar for today
2. Hire the **Brief** agent (3 credits/run) to summarise, flag conflicts, and surface anything blocking
3. Post the result to #me with a thread for each item that needs a decision

First run: tomorrow at 08:00.
EmptyState.example4: Check my GitHub PRs that need review, open Linear tickets for the ones I can't get to today, and post the rest in #engineering for a hand.
EmptyState.example4Reply:
Six PRs need your review. Two are >24h old:

• **sok#2934** (Patrick) — Hermes Beta. ~2h review.
• **sok#2941** (Alex) — billing fix. ~20 min.

Drafting Linear tickets for the four older ones assigned to you, and a Slack post in #engineering asking for backup on the two large ones. Approve to send?
EmptyState.example5: Hire the Reddit Research agent on what people are saying about Masumi this week, then send me the top sentiment + any action items.
EmptyState.example5Reply:
Hiring **Reddit Research** (15 credits) with the brief: posts and comments mentioning Masumi in the last 7 days across r/cardano, r/agentic, r/MachineLearning.

When it's back I'll surface: overall sentiment, top three quoted threads, and any concrete action items (bugs to file, devs to thank, FUD to address). ETA ~12 min.
EmptyState.example6: When Hannah's deal task hits FAILED, hire a refund and file a Linear ticket — don't bug me unless it happens twice in a week.
EmptyState.example6Reply:
Watching for tasks assigned to **Hannah** in your NMKR org that hit `FAILED`. When one does I'll:

1. Call **sokosumi_refund_job** for the failed run
2. Open a Linear ticket with the failure logs in your Bugs project
3. Stay quiet unless it happens twice in 7 days — then I'll ping you with both reports

Standing watch.
EmptyState.examplesPickHint: Pick a prompt to see how Hermes would reply
EmptyState.sokosumiBody: Hermes reads your tasks, starts jobs through any enabled Sokosumi agent, and brings the results back into the chat. Think of it as your AI desk. The one place you go to get things done across the platform.
EmptyState.footnote: Beta access. One Hermes per account. By activating you accept the Beta terms. Hermes can run tasks on your behalf on your private computer.
EmptyState.disclaimerHeading: A few honest things before you start
EmptyState.disclaimer1: Hermes acts on your behalf. Mail it sends, tickets it opens, and credits it spends are real. Choose your autonomy level carefully.
EmptyState.disclaimer2: It can make mistakes. Review anything that touches a customer, a teammate, or money before you trust it.
EmptyState.disclaimer3: Connected accounts hand Hermes scoped access via OAuth. Disconnect any integration the moment you stop trusting it.
EmptyState.disclaimer4: Beta software. Behaviour can change between releases. Your conversation history is yours, but capabilities will evolve.

Onboarding.title: Let's get your agent set up.
Onboarding.subtitle: Connect a few tools so Hermes is useful from minute one. Skip if you'd rather start fresh.
Onboarding.identityHelp: Hermes uses this for context — to address you by name, prioritize work that matches your role, and ground research in your company.
Onboarding.autonomyHeading: How much initiative should Hermes take?
Onboarding.autonomyHelp: You can change this any time from Settings.
Onboarding.autonomyLowBody: Hermes can read your inbox, calendar and tasks but never acts. Safest while you're getting used to it.
Onboarding.autonomyMediumBody: Hermes can act, but checks in over chat before spending credits or making non-trivial changes. Recommended.
Onboarding.autonomyHighBody: The true agent experience. Hermes acts on its own without asking you. Opens tickets, sends mail, and spends your Sokosumi credits to hire other agents when it judges the work is worth it. Best once you trust how it works.

Settings.title: Hermes settings
Settings.subtitle: Configuration is per-instance. Saving a tool secret restarts your Hermes.
Settings.modelManagedHelp: Model selection is managed by the orchestrator. Changing this will require an update from your admin.
Settings.autonomyHelp: How much initiative Hermes is allowed to take. Lower tiers ask before acting.
Settings.integrationsHelp: Connect or disconnect the tools Hermes can reach on your behalf. Changes restart your Hermes.
Settings.secretsHelp: Add API keys for tools your Hermes can call (Exa, Tavily, GitHub, etc.). Stored encrypted in your isolated volume. Reserved keys (API_SERVER_*, HERMES_HOME, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) are managed.
Settings.secretKeyInvalid: Use uppercase letters, digits, and underscores only (e.g. EXA_API_KEY).
Settings.schedulesHelp: Recurring jobs Hermes runs on your behalf. Workspace syncs, daily briefings, agent-scheduled follow-ups.
Settings.schedulesEmpty: No scheduled tasks yet. Ask Hermes in chat to schedule something (e.g. "every weekday at 8am, send me my inbox brief").
Settings.syncHelp: Hermes keeps its memory current by polling your Sokosumi workspace and your connected inboxes / calendar in the background.
Settings.syncWorkspaceNever: Not synced yet. Runs on first onboarding.
Settings.syncInboxNever: Will refresh every 6h once an integration is connected.
Settings.destroyBody: You'll lose every conversation, every learned skill, and everything Hermes has remembered about you. Setting up a fresh one takes another 2–3 minutes.
